raw_case_text:
A 43-year-old man, a resident of Uttar Pradesh, driver by occupation, a smoker for 25 years, and occasional alcohol consumer, having a previous history of dengue fever six years back, known patient of diabetes mellitus, presented with a history of acute onset intermittent, high-grade fever associated with chills during the last seven days followed by mild to moderate epigastric pain and two episodes of gum bleeding. He also noticed yellowish discoloration of eyes for three to four days, and throat pain for two days. On examination, the patient was hemodynamically stable with a random blood sugar of 180 mg/dL and had multiple ecchymoses over the arm and abdomen, icterus, and multiple creamy white patches over the tongue, posterior oro-pharyngeal wall and palate (Figures 2A, 2B). Tenderness was noted on the right hypochondriac region; on respiratory system examination, the patient had inspiratory crackles over bilateral infra-axillary and infra-scapular areas. The rest of the systemic examination was unremarkable.
Baseline blood investigation showed hematocrit of 39.7%, thrombocytopenia of 19,000/mm3, and total leukocyte count of 6,700/mm3; liver function test showed total bilirubin of 3.56 mg/dL, direct bilirubin of 2.00 mg/dL, SGPT of 450 Units/liter and SGOT of 633 Units/liter, with alkaline phosphatase of 559 Units/liter. The renal function test was within normal limits. A tropical fever workup came positive for dengue NS1 (ELISA method), and viral markers (anti-HCV, anti-HIV I/II, and HBsAg) were non-reactive. Serum HBA1C level was 10%. Fundoscopy showed no evidence of hypertensive or diabetic retinopathy, and urine routine microscopy showed no evidence of proteinuria. Abdominal ultrasonography showed grade II fatty liver with coarse liver echotexture without any sign of portal hypertension or dilatation of biliary radicle. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy showed evidence of oro-pharyngeal candidiasis but not esophageal involvement or any varices there.
The patient improved with conservative management and transfusion of random donor platelets. Oral thrush improved with nystatin suspension, 4 mL four times a day. Over the next two weeks, the patient reported a complete resolution of throat pain. Blood glucose was optimized using subcutaneous regular insulin (10U three times a day) in the outpatient setting.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 43-year-old male presented with high-grade fever with chills for 7 days, epigastric pain, gum bleeding, jaundice for 3-4 days, and sore throat for 2 days.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with a 7-day history of acute intermittent high-grade fever with chills, followed by mild to moderate epigastric pain and two episodes of gingival bleeding. Over the preceding 3-4 days, he noted scleral icterus, and developed progressive odynophagia over the past 2 days.
subjective.past_medical_history: Known history of type 2 diabetes mellitus. Documented acute febrile illness 6 years prior. Driver by occupation residing in Uttar Pradesh, India. 25-pack-year smoking history and occasional alcohol consumption.
subjective.review_of_systems: Reported fever, chills, epigastric discomfort, gingival bleeding, jaundice, and sore throat. Denied melena, hematemesis, or altered sensorium.

objective.physical_examination: Patient was hemodynamically stable. Scleral icterus was noted. Cutaneous examination showed multiple ecchymoses over the arms and abdomen. Oropharyngeal examination revealed multiple creamy white plaques over the tongue, posterior oropharyngeal wall, and soft palate. Abdominal examination demonstrated right hypochondrial tenderness without peritoneal signs. Respiratory examination revealed inspiratory crackles over bilateral infra-axillary and infra-scapular areas.
objective.routine_investigations:
Complete blood count: Hematocrit 39.7%, platelet count 19,000/mm3, total leukocyte count 6,700/mm3.
Liver function tests: Total bilirubin 3.56 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 2.00 mg/dL, SGOT 633 U/L, SGPT 450 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 559 U/L.
Renal function tests: Within normal limits.
Metabolic profile: Random blood glucose 180 mg/dL, HbA1c 10%.
Urinalysis: Normal without proteinuria.
Abdominal ultrasonography: Grade II hepatic steatosis with coarse echotexture; no evidence of portal hypertension or intrahepatic/extrahepatic biliary dilatation.
objective.advanced_workup:
Fundoscopy: No diabetic or hypertensive retinopathy.
Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy: Oropharyngeal candidiasis confirmed; no esophageal candidiasis or gastroesophageal varices.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Severe dengue fever with hemorrhagic manifestations (gum bleeding, ecchymoses), severe thrombocytopenia, hepatic dysfunction, secondary oropharyngeal candidiasis, and uncontrolled type 2 diabetes mellitus. Confirmed by positive dengue NS1 antigen test (ELISA). Viral serologies for HIV I/II, HCV, and HBV (HBsAg) were non-reactive.
Treatment and outcome: Treated with supportive care and transfusion of random donor platelets. Oral candidiasis was successfully treated with oral nystatin suspension (4 mL four times daily), leading to complete resolution of odynophagia within 2 weeks. Diabetes was managed with regular subcutaneous insulin (10 units three times daily).
